items.fullSentence: Je prends la ligne 4 jusqu'à Montparnasse.

whyWrong.prend: prend is the il/elle form — with je it's prends.
whyWrong.prenons: prenons is the nous form — with je it's prends.
whyWrong.pris: pris is the past participle — the present with je is prends.

items.fullSentence: Pour aller à l'Opéra, vous prenez la ligne 3.
items.sentenceTrans: To get to the Opéra, you take line 3.

whyWrong.prenons: prenons is the nous form — with vous it's prenez.
whyWrong.prennent: prennent is the ils/elles form — with vous it's prenez.
whyWrong.prend: prend is the il/elle form — with vous it's prenez.

items.fullSentence: Nous prenons le métro tous les jours.
items.sentenceTrans: We take the metro every day.

whyWrong.prends: prends is the je/tu form — with nous it's prenons.
whyWrong.prennent: prennent is the ils/elles form — with nous it's prenons.
whyWrong.prenez: prenez is the vous form — with nous it's prenons.

items.fullSentence: Je vais à l'université en bus.
items.sentenceTrans: I go to university by bus.

whyWrong.à: à is only used for à pied / à vélo — enclosed transport takes en: en bus.
whyWrong.au: au (à + le) adds an article that isn't used here — it's en bus.
whyWrong.avec: avec means 'with' — 'by bus' is en bus.

items.fullSentence: Elle va au marché à pied.
items.sentenceTrans: She goes to the market on foot.

whyWrong.en: en is for vehicles you get inside — 'on foot' is the fixed à pied.
whyWrong.au: au (à + le) adds an article — the fixed phrase is à pied.
whyWrong.par: par means 'by/through' — 'on foot' is à pied.

items.sentenceBefore: — On va à la plage ? — Oui, on
items.fullSentence: — On va à la plage ? — Oui, on y va demain.
items.sentenceTrans: — Are we going to the beach? — Yes, we're going there tomorrow.

whyWrong.là: là is an adverb 'there' — it can't sit before the verb here; the pronoun is y.
whyWrong.le: le is a direct-object pronoun — à la plage is replaced by y.
whyWrong.en: en replaces de + noun — à la plage (à + place) is replaced by y.

items.fullSentence: Ce café ? J'y vais souvent le matin.
items.sentenceTrans: This café? I often go there in the morning.

whyWrong.en: en replaces de + noun — à ce café (à + place) is replaced by y.
whyWrong.le: le is a direct-object pronoun — a place introduced by à is replaced by y.
whyWrong.me: me means 'me/to me' — the place pronoun is y.

items.fullSentence: Les touristes prennent beaucoup de photos.
items.sentenceTrans: The tourists take a lot of photos.

whyWrong.prend: Les touristes is plural — ils prennent.
whyWrong.prenons: That's the nous form — ils prennent.

items.fullSentence: On va y aller la semaine prochaine.
items.sentenceTrans: We're going to go there next week.

whyWrong.là: là can't sit between va and aller — the pronoun y goes before the infinitive.
whyWrong.le: le replaces a thing — a place with à takes y.
whyWrong.en: en replaces de + noun — going TO a place is y.

items.fullSentence: Je n'y vais pas encore cette année.
items.sentenceTrans: I'm not going there yet this year.

whyWrong.y ne: ne comes before y — n'y vais pas.
whyWrong.n'en: en replaces de + noun — the place is y.
